title: Galaxy S5 lacks keyboard chooser; switching Polished Recognition is tedious.
summary: # Galaxy S5 lacks keyboard chooser; switching Polished Recognition is tedious. I have no way to get the keyboard chooser on my old Galaxy S5 because the NAF hardware buttons are implemented, so the old Android version doesn’t show a keyboard chooser. How should I handle this? We have a Settings gear icon, but it only displays a pointless dialog that tells us to open Settings from the launcher. The real problem is that on the Galaxy it’s very cumbersome: I have to launch Polished Recognition from the launcher, scroll down to “Enable Voice Keyboard,” and then turn off Polished Recognition there. It’s a tedious job to switch smoothly between keyboards. Polished Recognition now acts as a keyboard, but I still need to be able to switch back quickly to a keyboard that allows typing.
